utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Call the case, please, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case number IT-98-34-T, the Prosecutor versus Naletilic and Martinovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Could we have the witness, please? Yes, Mr. Krsnik?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, good morning, very briefly, I merely wish to tell you that yesterday we wrote a motion which we filed this morning, which has to do with our suggestion regarding the final witnesses in Mladen Naletilic case, and our suggestion is to organise for a week before the holidays, to organise the videolink for all those who were to testify through depositions and Mr. Martinovic's Defence can start on the 15th as planned. I merely wish to inform thaw we wrote that motion yesterday and filed it today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: And we will render our decisions after receiving your motion. Mr. Scott, are you going to reply to this motion or you may do it orally.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Your Honour, we haven't received it yet so when we have a chance to look at it we'll make a response. It may be that depending on the motion we can just respond orally once we have had a chance to review it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, Mr. Seric?

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. Very briefly, Mr. Martinovic's Defence can go along with Mr. Naletilic's Defence but we'd like to know what is your decision as soon as possible so that we could organise the arrival of our witnesses, because it doesn't -- it does make a difference if it will be ten or 15 days, whether we will have ten or 15 working days because the number of witnesses will also depend on that of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I believe that the other day, I've already said that your case will start on the 15th of July, and at this moment, we are getting in touch with the Registrar to arrange the time and facilities for the videolink witnesses in the Naletilic case. So as soon as we get the specific reply from the Registrar, we will make the decision in this aspect. Yes. Could we have the witness, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Good morning, Witness. You may sit down, please. Yes, Mr. Prosecutor, you may continue with your cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Your Honour. Cross-examined by Mr. Poriouvaev: [Continued]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness NP, is it correct that the first volunteers to the regiment Kralj Tomislav was established in July 1992 in Opuzen? Excuse me pronunciation of the location.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NP [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor, Kralj Tomislav volunteer regiment was based at Cepikuce and its first headquarters was in Opuzen, and then in January, it moved to Vrgorac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it correct that Ludvig Pavlovic unit was created on the basis of these first volunteer regiment?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NP [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ludvig Pavlovic was made of the former members of the Kralj Tomislav volunteer regiment, Croats, Bosniaks and new members who joined in Capljina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, was the first regiment -- I mean Kralj Tomislav, a HV or an HVO unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NP [Resumed]
utterances.text: Kralj Tomislav volunteer regiment was a unit of the Croatian Army in the Republic of Croatia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it correct that it was commanded, I mean the 1st regiment was commanded by brigadier Mate Sarlija or Daidza?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NP [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it correct that Bozan Simovic was his deputy?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NP [Resumed]
utterances.text: Bozan Simovic commanded a battalion in the Kralj Tomislav regiment. General Daidza did not have a deputy.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it correct that the regiment was disbanded in April, 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NP [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It was disbanded at a later date. I do not know exactly when. After Ludvig Pavlovic was established, then General Daidza formed another regiment, I believe it was called Nihad Kulenovic and it was either in Jablanica or in Konjic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it correct that some of the members of the former 1st Regiment joined the new unit created by Daidza and the other part of soldiers departed with Bozan Simovic to Capljina?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NP [Resumed]
utterances.text: The majority of members went to Capljina with Bozan Simovic and Nihad Kulenovic was made of new members and a very small number of men from the former regiment, from the former Kralj Tomislav Regiment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which part of the former 1st Regiment did you join?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NP [Resumed]
utterances.text: I joined the former part, the one which later on set up the Ludvig Pavlovic unit, but at Daidza's request I went to Bosnia with him several times.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it correct that Capljina municipal authorities allowed the unit which would be called Ludvig Pavlovic later to use the Gabela Barracks?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NP [Resumed]
utterances.text: The authorities in Capljina allowed the Ludvig Pavlovic unit to use the barracks in Gabela only after the large barracks in Capljina was liberated.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it correct that somewhere in December, 1992, your unit had somewhere around 118 soldiers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NP [Resumed]
utterances.text: Possibly. I do not know the exact number, but yes, it's about that size.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: I would like the usher to put before -- in front of the witness Exhibit number 206.1.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, I would like you to look down the document and direct your attention to item B, which contains the description of Ludvig Pavlovic unit.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NP [Resumed]
utterances.text: I read it, Mr. Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you may also take a look at some diagrams here, table, on the second page of this. There is some diagram.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NP [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And to the effect that Ludvig Pavlovic had 118 soldiers in December, 1992.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NP [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Sir, does this description of Ludvig Pavlovic unit correspond to the real situation in which Ludvig Pavlovic unit found itself in December, 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NP [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Prosecutor, I'm glad to have read this, but I cannot make assessments of my unit, but it could be true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: For example, it was well equipped materially and well trained, is it correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NP [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that is not quite correct. It was far from outstanding military organisation but in relation to other units, we were well organised. As for the equipment, all that we captured, we did not sell it, we kept it and then distributed it amongst the members of the unit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. So is it your testimony that most of the soldiers were former HV soldiers?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krsnik?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I wish to draw your attention and I'd like to ask -- I waited to finish with this document, because we have adopted a new rule not to stand up whilst the document is still being discussed, namely this document, 206.1 which now emerges as a new document from the Zagreb archive and it is a very interesting document. I'd like to know when did OTD get it because this document says loudly and clearly, several things. First, that the Convicts Battalion was commanded by Mario Hrkac, that ATG Baja Kraljevic was commanded by --

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: I would object.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I finish? Just a moment. You can object but it's my turn now. So you wait until I finish.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Krsnik, do not touch upon the contents of this document until the witness is gone, and you may make objections about authenticity of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Krsnik, I believe you still have the opportunity during your re-examination, if you are going to touch upon the contents of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, of course, Your Honours. I respect every decision that you make and I will do so this time. I merely wish to say such assertions when we had witnesses from the Prosecution did not exist and the Prosecutor spoke in front of the witnesses whatever he liked to and whenever I stood up and requested that the witness be taken out, that it should not be said in front of the witness, the witness nevertheless stayed in and the Prosecutor behaved in this way and I do not see what this witness has to do with my objection about an exculpatory document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Krsnik, I've already said that you may challenge the authenticity of this document at this moment but do not Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. touch upon the contents of that document while the witness is here. We will give you the opportunity at a later stage when this document is submitted for admission.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I am not trying to question its authenticity. My question was when did the OTP enter into possession of this document because this is an exculpatory document and when is it that they got this document. That was all but we can leave it until a later stage. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Shall I reply? Or there is no need?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: First of all, we are well aware of our ongoing obligation to disclose all exculpatory documents and we are doing that as soon as new documents are coming in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Sorry for cutting across here, the point you're making, Mr. Krsnik, is a very valid point and we picked it up immediately. What is sauce for the goose is sauce for the Gander, if Mr. Krsnik can't discuss did in front of the witness, neither can the Prosecution. We would be very happy to have a discussion about this document when the witness lass completed his evidence. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Thank you very much. It makes things easier, for me at least.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I would ask the Trial Chamber to move to private session for some moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, we will go to the private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, we are in the open session.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you give me a response?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NP [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mate Boban, I received, that is we received, on the 6th of June, and that is the day when we were founded, and the battalion had 500 men on its strength.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When was it called "Independent HVO Battalion"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NP [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was called "the unit for special purposes Ludvig Pavlovic" by its establishment it was supposed to be of the strength of a battalion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it correct that on the 23rd of August, 1992, this battalion was called Ludvig Pavlovic? Could you explain to the Trial Chamber what stands for Ludvig Pavlovic, who stands for Ludvig Pavlovic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NP [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ludvig Pavlovic was born in Ljubuski. He was an emigrant. He returned to Bosnia-Herzegovina with a group of people. He was in prison, he was liberated in 1990, and in 1991, he was killed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Maybe now for reasons of safety, we should return to closed session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, we will go back to the private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, would it be fair to say that the HVO command was prepared for the events of the 9th of May, which occurred in Mostar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NP [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't say that it was very prepared, because there had been too -- there were too many victims, too many casualties, but in any case, even before that, there were some prepatory commands, alerts, because of the events that had taken place in Central Bosnia and in Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: I would like the witness to be shown Exhibit 365.1.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you familiar with this order?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NP [Resumed]
utterances.text: May I please read it? I've read it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So were you aware of this order?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NP [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not remember this order. I don't believe that Mr. Petkovic signed it, because I never split my units.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But do you agree that your unit was ready on the basis of this order or some other order, to intervene in some military actions? In May, 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NP [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It would have been if it was not engaged in combat elsewhere.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Isn't it your statement that your unit was also involved in the military operations in Mostar on the 9th and 10th of May, 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NP [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I explained yesterday how we arrived and how we joined the fighting in Mostar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember approximately at what time you received a signal, information, about the events in Mostar on the 9th of May?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NP [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember exactly. It was early in the morning. The duty operations officer woke me up. I only remember that it was very early in the morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long did it take you to get from Capljina to Mostar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NP [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I was explaining things yesterday, I told you that with the intervention unit in passenger vehicles and in jeeps, we headed off for Mostar and it took us about an hour via Citluk, we couldn't go via Mostar because the Bosniaks had occupied Mahala.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So at what time did you arrive in Mostar, approximately?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NP [Resumed]
utterances.text: That really depends on the time when I started. I believe that it was sometime between 7.00 and 8.00.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see Mr. Lasic personally on that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NP [Resumed]
utterances.text: On that day, I saw Mr. Lasic on several occasions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it him who communicated his order to you, and determined your role in Mostar military operation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NP [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I believe it was somebody from the Main Staff, because when I arrived, Mr. Lasic was not there. I believe -- this gentleman was an elderly gentleman, either Slavko Puljic or another Chief of the Main Staff. I can't remember exactly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you arrived in Mostar, was the fighting under way already?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NP [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Mostar was aflame, literally aflame. There were many civilians, women, children, men, who were roaming around the town and fleeing the places where the fighting was underway.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see from the Rondo area, where you were deployed at that time, that Vranica building was already ablaze?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NP [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not stationed at the Rondo. At first, I was not at Rondo. I went straight from Bijeli Brijeg towards Vranica and towards the dormitory, students' residence building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was the building ablaze?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NP [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it your statement that it was ABiH who attacked HVO on the 9th of May?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NP [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How do you know that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NP [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is what they told me. I was not in Mostar. They told me that on the previous day, on that day, they killed some people, some policemen, they captured some people, took them prisoner.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Whom do you mean by "they"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NP [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean the command of the Mostar Corps.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So it is not your personal knowledge, it's the information that you got from others, right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NP [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe I explained that I was stationed in Capljina, that I wasn't in Mostar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: I would like the witness to be shown Exhibit 374.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This SpaBat Intrep, filed on the 9th of May, 1993. Yes. It also has a B/C/S version. Page 34. Just not relevant to Mostar. We will take a look, a quick look at this part of the document. Do you see that at 5.00, mortar attacks were launched against the Muslim sector from HVO positions?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NP [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I've read that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you agree that the information that you had got on that day, on the initiator of the attack might have been wrong?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NP [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't agree. I've read on, and it says that the building housing the command of the 41st Brigade of the army is ablaze. I don't know what building is that. There is the building of the 4th Corps.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Maybe it might have been wrong interpreted by SpaBat but it was the Vranica building?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NP [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. It's possible.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Is it your testimony that you were given platoon -- a platoon from the 3rd Brigade and as a reserve, Juka's unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NP [Resumed]
utterances.text: The platoon from the 3rd Brigade had already been deployed there and Juka was given to us as a reserve in case we needed anybody.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you need him?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, we are not receiving the Croatian interpretation. I understood it but the witness has not received the interpretation in B/C/S, of the last question, that is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Prosecutor, would you please try that again?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you need Juka's unit during the operation of the 9th and 10th of May in Mostar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NP [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Later on, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When? What do you mean by "later"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NP [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first time they helped me when we were breaking through from Rondo, from the Rondo area, and the second time during the fierce battles around Vranica on the second day because him and his group had a lot of experience in fighting within town. That experience he got in Sarajevo where he was one of the best-known defendants of Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he under your command, under your direct command?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NP [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were equal. I was the commander of the independent unit. He was also the commander of an independent unit. But when he got there, he would turn to me and ask for orders.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you give orders to him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NP [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not really. I would actually inform him. I would put him in the picture, and if there was a need, he would join the fighting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it correct that on the following day, I mean the 10th of May, the 4th HVO Brigade Stjepan Radic was placed under your command?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NP [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: I would like the witness to be shown Exhibit 376.1.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I've read it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you agree that such kind of order existed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NP [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't agree. It may have been written by somebody but I really -- I never saw it, nor was this unit placed under my command, ever. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was in the overall command of the military operation in Mostar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NP [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor, the commander of the operation zone Eastern Herzegovina was Mr. Miljenko Lasic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm well aware of it but who was in command of the operation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NP [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've told you already, at least who I received my orders from.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So it was Miljenko Lasic, right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NP [Resumed]
utterances.text: My immediate commander was Miljenko Lasic, and I don't know whether his commander may have been Miljenko Petkovic. That I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My next question will be is it your testimony that it were you, your soldiers, and Juka's soldiers who were searching Vranica building after it had been secured?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NP [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The Vranica building was searched by myself. I first checked whether there were any booby traps, any mines, and after that, I collected the archives and all the other documents. Juka Prazina was outside and he was the one who took over the prisoners.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And yesterday, during the examination-in-chief, you claimed that you told Juka to escort prisoners taken from Vranica building on the 10th of May, to military police, and you also stated that you think that he did so. But do you really know if he escorted them to the military police?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NP [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor, I said yesterday that I headed towards the ministry building to hand over the archives, and that I asked for permission to move my unit towards Capljina. I did that, and about half an hour later, I moved my unit towards Capljina. I did not do any subsequent checkings.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But do you know that 12 prisoners taken out of Vranica building have never been seen alive?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krsnik?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, could we have the foundation for this? And I'm asking for it because the Prosecutor knows very well indeed, he is well aware, that for this incident, a man has been brought to justice in Mostar, at their orders, and I do not know why is he inviting this witness to speculate. And whether they are missing or not, nobody is known to this day. These are speculative questions necessitating speculative answers, and the OTP knows very well that there is a case in Mostar against a man at the orders of this -- of this OTP, and he's the head of the -- the chief of the Mostar police who is now on trial.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: May I reply, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: We had a number of witnesses here in the courtroom who claimed that those people were never seen alive. That's what I claim. That's what I ask this witness to respond. There is no speculation at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: And this witness was there at that moment, and he might know, and he might not know about that fact. Who knows? We will hear the answer from this witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, yesterday I spoke about two groups of prisoners. This group of how many, 12 men, was not taken from Vranica. It was captured in the area between Vranica and Rondo. I also said that from the contact zone, we went away and then returned to it, so that I really do not know about it. And I do not know about these next group. I said we had no conditions to keep prisoners.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Is it correct that you saw Mladen Naletilic on the 10th of May in front of the Ministry of Defence?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krsnik?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, merely to inform you that I do not have to copy the documents, and then translate them for you. Have you finished your previous question? I have to ask the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Yes, I'm making a second question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This has to do with the previous question about those 12 men. There is, and there was completed, the investigation, the first instance judgement was passed, and the case is in the appeals court, and that was all done on the orders of this Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Krsnik, I don't see any connections for your explanation in this aspect. I think the Prosecution has asked that question and the witness has already answered that already. We are not charging anybody in this Tribunal about the fate of that 12 men at this stage. Let's move on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So my question was: Do you confirm that you saw Mr. Naletilic on the 10th of May in front of the Ministry of Defence?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NP [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he alone?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NP [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've already said that there were -- that the whole area was awash with people, civilians and soldiers, and when I approached and started to tell Juka not to hit his acquaintance. He came -- Juka came to me and asked me how was it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NP [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not know how to explain. There was a lot of people there, whether somebody had come with him or whether he was alone there, I do not know but there were indeed very many people there. Because I do not know whether he had come with somebody else.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see Miljenko Lasic at that time together with Mladen Naletilic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NP [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think so. It was a long time ago but I think not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... Zeljko Bosnjak?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NP [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which Zeljko Bosnjak?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Don't you know that person?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NP [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, no. I know several Zeljko Bosnjaks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see any of them in front of the Ministry of Defence, on that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NP [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not remember, Mr. Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Did you ever participate in any other military operations together with Juka Prazina?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NP [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not recall that I cooperated with him ever again but I did see him on a couple of occasions again, once again we were in Mostar, he came there too and came to say hello.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see him in the area of Prozor?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NP [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yesterday, my learned colleague's question, to whom Jusuf Prazina was subordinate remained unanswered. Maybe you'll give a reply to this question today.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I object. The witness yesterday answered that question when I asked him, and I think it will be fair, I do not know what is in the transcript but the witness has answered this. But I did not check the transcript so I cannot say how it was reflected in the transcript. But he answered that question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, it doesn't matter that the witness answered that question again. So far as I remember, I could not recall any answer from this witness. So I'm interested to hear what the witness is going to tell us.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I believe that Juka Prazina was a kind of a special purpose unit, that was I suppose his condition, to join the HVO units, but I do not know how -- he was quite independent from what I could see.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would it be correct to say that Juka Prazina unit had the name of Krusko Convicts Battalion unit was subordinate to Mr. Mladen Naletilic?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krsnik?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Prosecutor -- could the Prosecutor repeat the name of the unit? Because the interpreters could not hear the name of the unit and they told us so. So could the name of the unit be repeated?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, we didn't get it in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Krusko Convicts Battalion. K-R-U-S-K-O. I would like the witness to be shown Exhibit 494. Could you read this document?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NP [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is a request signed by Mr. Andabak over Mladen Naletilic's name, do you agree that it is a request of commander for his subordinate unit to get some military equipment, sorry, to get some telephone connection?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krsnik?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, the Prosecutor cannot know who is signing something on behalf of whom. He can do it -- only do that if he can show a document but he can not say -- the Prosecutor does not know who signed what on behalf of whom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Krsnik, we are not talking about a document at this moment. And we don't have this document at our hands, Mr. Prosecutor, so we are in a disadvantaged position to judge this matter. I did not find that document in that bundle you furnished to us.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Just a moment. You will have it in a second. The documents were distributed this morning.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: You gave me one set this morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: All right, Your Honour, I have completed this set Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. of questions. Maybe it's wise to make a break now. It's time I think. Or maybe I'm wrong.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krsnik?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, just for the sake of my conscience, for the record, for fairness, it is not possible to allow three times as much time for the cross-examination as for the direct because I really may not finish by the 15th of July. Your Honours, I examined for 40 minutes and the Prosecutor has been examining for one hour and a half, four times longer than I have. I kept my mouth shut, I kept my mouth shut but I think it's really more than enough.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: May I reply?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Prosecutor, I think you've spent 30 minutes on the issues that it seems to us there is no dispute at all between both parties. Could I ask you at this moment how long are you going to take to finish your cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Your Honour, I will need maybe another 30 minutes, because the counsel covered in his direct examination questions not indicated in the summaries. That's why I had to make some additional preparations, prepare some additional documents, to contest his allegations. That's the reason why I had to, and I ask you to give me some more time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I understand that at this moment of the cross-examination, you came to the central matters of this case. And I believe that it's very important for us to hear what the witness says about your answer. We will give you another 30 minutes after the break.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We will rise until quarter to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Prosecutor, please continue.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So, witness, my last question was if you know that Juka Prazina unit was subordinate to Convicts Battalion and to Mladen Naletilic as its commander?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NP [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor, I do not know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. You don't know. Let's move to another question. Then you also claimed yesterday that you don't remember if Mr. Naletilic had a pistol about him on the 10th of May, right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NP [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right, yes. I am not sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Is it your testimony that Ludvig Pavlovic unit was involved in military operation in Rastani before the 23rd of September, 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NP [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, once.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you personally participate in this operation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NP [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember the approximate date of that operation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NP [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, Mr. Prosecutor. It was summer but I couldn't be more precise.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And what were the tasks given to your unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NP [Resumed]
utterances.text: My -- defence lines in Rastani were under threat so our task was to take -- to look after the most vulnerable point, and it was some industrial facility, a silo or something like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it correct that when your unit entered the village, it had already been secured by some other units? I mean HVO units.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NP [Resumed]
utterances.text: Members of the Mostar Brigade were there. I don't know whether it was the 2nd or the 3rd Brigade which was in that area. And Mr. Stampar, I believe it was, who took us to the line.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were your tasks to replace those units in Rastani?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NP [Resumed]
utterances.text: My task was first and foremost to secure -- to secure, to guard, that worst, that most sensitive place and members of that brigade were there with me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you entered the village did you see the houses burned down?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NP [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were houses which had already burnt down. They were not aflame at the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see corpses of killed soldiers and civilians in Rastani?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NP [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Only far away from the front line we could see in a meadow between houses, we could see somebody lying down.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever get to know that the day before, at least 11 civilians had been summarily executed in Rastani?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NP [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sorry, day before? What day? Day before I got there or -- ?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, yes, the day before you entered the village.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krsnik?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, could we ask the Prosecutor what is that operation that he's talking about? What is that operation that he has in mind? When was that and what is he examining this witness about? As far as I know, we have the operations on the 23rd of September, according to the indictment, and the Prosecutor says it was in summer. Now, the 23rd of September is definitely not summer. So could we know what the Prosecutor is talking about?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Prosecutor would you please clarify this for us?

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: The witness yesterday claimed that he had never met Convicts Battalion in any military operations. That's the reason of my question. And now I will propose some documents, just to expose my case to this witness. I would like the witness to be shown Exhibits 575, 576.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: These are two orders of a similar content signed by chief of the Main Staff, Zarko Tole and signed for brigadier Miljenko Lasic. Are you familiar with these orders?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NP [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, Mr. Prosecutor. My orders were different. I received my orders regarding the engagement in Rastani from the Main Staff.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But do you see Ludvig Pavlovic unit indicated in these two orders?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NP [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So your position is that it's not true that you were to replace Convicts Battalion and Makini Ljudi units?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NP [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor, I've already told you that I came to replace the 2nd Brigade units but not in general, only at the most delicate place. If a maximum of men [as interpreted] from in Bijelo Polje, they were there, I did not see those of the Convicts Battalion, though.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right, witness. Your position is clear to me. My next question will be that is it correct that on the 23rd of September, 1993, you were appointed -- sorry, we should go into private session now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, we will go to the private session, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So were you aware of this document in your position that you occupied at that time? And particularly, that a mop up of the terrain in Golubic was carried out by Tuta ATG unit? And that the operation was successful and there were no losses of the positions on Golubic and they were taken by a group of Vitez, Ranko Boban Brigade and HV Croatian Army?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NP [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor, I have never seen this document. I was not aware of this operation. So I can't tell you anything about it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Witness, is it correct that Ludvig Pavlovic, throughout 1993 and afterwards, was a part of the HV, the Croatian Army?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NP [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Ludvig Pavlovic Battalion was on the strength of the Croatian Defence Council and its members, a number of them, were volunteers of the war in Croatia from its beginning, from 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: I would like the witness to be shown Exhibit P261.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What are your comments on this document?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NP [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were sent by Mr. Colonel Ivica Primorac and they were sent to the police administration in Zagreb.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm asking about the necessity for your soldiers to get the Croatian citizenship because the unit has the status of the unit of the Croatian Army; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NP [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor, it says here that they need these documents in order to regulate their status in the Croatian Army. This was done on the 12th of March. This document is dated the 12th of March. A number of people in mid-1993 left the Ludvig Pavlovic, the Bosniaks joined the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina. A smaller number remained with us. And members of the former regiment decided to go back to the Republic of Croatia because those who were volunteers starting with 1991 had certain -- enjoyed certain privileges in the Republic of Croatia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. That's quite clear but I will send you just to the beginning, to the second -- just line of the document. "Members of the special purposes unit of the Croatian Army."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NP [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It is correct. Members -- some, not many of them, some people, wanted to go back to the Republic of Croatia and in order to exercise their privilege of the fighters from the first day. So these privileges were getting an apartment, then retirement, early retirement.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I must cut you off because it's clear, but I'm asking you about Ludvig Pavlovic as a unit of the Croatian Army, as stated in this document.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NP [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor, we were not a unit of the Croatian Army. We never received any combat order or any other order for that matter from them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would like the usher to show the witness Exhibit 3 -- 433.1. The document issued in June, 1993, and it deals with one of the members of the unit, unit, who is a member of a unit with status of independent battalion of the Croatian Army, and this document, as it follows from it -- from its text was born within your unit. Is it correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NP [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Prosecutor. According to the memorandum on the appearance and the seal of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, it does derive from my -- it does originate from my unit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Let's pass on to document 718.1. This is a list of commissioned and non-commissioned HV officers. The document issued in December, 1993. In the first table, there are -- in the first list, sorry, there are eight -- 18 names. In the second, 46 names, right? And now I would like the Trial Chamber to move to a private session for some minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, we will go to the private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krsnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I do not know any more what strength we have, what strength I have to invest into my objections, especially to the last one by the learned friend Mr. Scott, because all my time was always counted in. Of course, the Honourable Court can always intervene during the examination by either side, and are we now to count the time down to a minute? Your Honours, I examined for 40 minutes. Look now at the time. It is half past 11.00. I've lost it. I meant to finish another witness today. And start with a third one. I do not know how this will proceed. Your Honours, perhaps today I will give it a thought and see whether it serves any purpose because I bring a fact witness and then for two hours we listen to whatever the Prosecutors wish to do, bringing heaps of these papers, because these are just papers, and we had to wait until they think they've satisfied whatever they were pursuing. Now, the examination you forget that it started yesterday, and that the Prosecutor spent 15 or 20 minutes yesterday, and now from 9.00 until half past 11.00, so let us calculate all the time that we spent. It is five or six times longer than I used for my direct examination. Sorry. And moreover, why doesn't the Honourable Court prohibit all the irrelevant questions rather than have the Prosecutor spend two hours on some irrelevant matters to come to something which is relevant? And then again time is wasted. And I really don't know where all this is leading. I do not think that this is correct. At least in my book. I know that you're trying your best and that you are showing a lot of understand and wisdom. You have given ample demonstration of that so far. But please, I am really most vehemently objecting because according to me, it is not fair, it is not just, and I'm sure I wouldn't be allowed and you didn't allow me during my cross-examination to do what is being done now. Thank you very much for giving me the floor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecution, try to wind up your cross-examination as soon as possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So, Witness, you have Exhibit 7440.2 in front of you, right? Take a look at the letterhead, in the left side, upper corner. Please would you read it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NP [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Croatian Army, Split military district, 60th" not the 16th but the 60th Battalion, Ludvig Pavlovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So what --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NP [Resumed]
utterances.text: Reference number Vrgorac 12th January, 1994, reference, certificate.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No need to read it further. What are your comments? Was your unit a part of the Croatian Army at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NP [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, allow me to explain it more extensively. Perhaps I might be on the right track to find some solution to this and to cut all this short.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. This is an important issue. You may make your explanations to this Court.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Your Honour. But let me answer the Prosecutor first. This is not my signature. The stamp and all the rest that you have here. Your Honours, when the members of the Ludvig Pavlovic who were in the Croatian Army voiced their wish to return to Croatia because a number of them had been born there, they had no other possibility to exercise their rights because the General Daidza had disbanded the volunteer regiment Kralj Tomislav. The principal act that needs to be, should somebody, so that he can exercise his rights is an acts on the membership and the time served with a particular unit. General Daidza made this seal, and you see that Vrgorac was the head quarters of the volunteer regiment and it is made that it is also the seat of the 60th Battalion, Ludvig Pavlovic. He told me about this and I was aware of the existence of this, and through this, he issued documents to those who had to resolve their status. Personally, this Ivica Zeljko or Zeljko, I do not know, he was never in my unit. So that if we want to say that we were not members of the Croatian Army, because had I been one, if I were attached to the Main Staff of the Croat Defence Council, then it could take a month or two, but there was no way in which it could last five years. I suppose that the Prosecutor will have more such papers, but I tried in this way to tell you whence this unit. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: I would like the witness to be shown Exhibit 761.1.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I've read it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was this letter signed by you? Is it your signature?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NP [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you -- take a look at the letterhead again.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NP [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was the first thing I read.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But is it your signature?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NP [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I told you so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... sorry. Did you send this letter to Mr. Bobetko?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NP [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor, do you really believe that I could communicate with General Bobetko at that time?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you mean this letter is forged?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NP [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. This is an original document, except that it was taken to Zagreb by General Daidza and I have to explain it to you. General Daidza was the first legendary hero of the war, and he had doors wide open to President Tudjman or wherever.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it correct that in this letter, you request the general staff of the Croatian Army to pay salaries to your soldiers from the funds of the Croatian Army?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NP [Resumed]
utterances.text: We complained because in the HVO, our salaries were lower than the salaries in the Croatian Army, but the HVO had less funds, and the most important thing, and most important thing is that salaries were always overdue in the Croat Defence Council. We did get our salaries from the HVO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why did you ask for salaries from HV? From the army of independent state which had nothing to do, as you claim, with your country and your military forces?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NP [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor, I think that at about this time, the Washington Agreement was signed. We wanted on the basis of the status that we enjoyed before, we wanted to try to get our salaries from Croatia, because it was a better regulated state and it had higher salaries. However, that was not done.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But, Witness, Germany was far more better regulated state. Why didn't you address Germany for salary then, if you follow your logic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NP [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because I did not fight in the German army or for the German state.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But did you fight for the Croatian Army, for the Republic of Croatia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NP [Resumed]
utterances.text: I personally, a little less so, but some of my members were in the Croatian Army from 1991, and they were at the worst fronts, from Cepikuce, to Pakrac, Lipik, everywhere, and they are still -- and they are still top guys who are in the street. Had we got this from the Croatian Army, they would be getting some money now, wouldn't have to do all sorts of odd jobs.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this point, I must just to wind up and I will ask some more questions but we should go into private session now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, we will go to the private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I merely like to take the numbers of all the documents I want to use. I believe it will speed matters up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Krsnik, why don't we break here and give you more time to sort out all those documents and furnish that list to the Registrar so that they could be prepared?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I agree.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. So we'll resume at 20 past 12.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Seric?

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Mr. President. I did not want to waste your time during the cross-examination, and in Mr. Krsnik objected whenever it was necessary, but it is my duty to my client and the record of this main hearing, it is my duty to say that Mr. Krsnik is quite right when he objected insistently against the duration of the cross-examination. This Defence was not allowed by the Chamber to go beyond the time of the direct examination, in our cross-examination. And we were being interrupted and told that we had already heard answers during the direct examination, whereas the Prosecutor does it all the time and we spend 45 minutes to one hour repeating questions, the answers to which we have already heard during the direct examination, thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Scott?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, I'm primarily address other things, but just a brief response, both to Mr. Seric and to similar points that have been raised by Mr. Krsnik before. Your Honour, I think the record will show in this case, I'm quite confident respectfully, I submitted, the record it in case will show quite clearly that there was full and extensive cross-examination by the Defence in the Prosecution case. I think the Chamber will remember collectively that the three of you, that the cross-examination of a number of Prosecution witnesses went on for at substantial length and again, I'm confident that full and fair cross-examination was afforded to counsel. Mr. President, on another matter, in terms of the motion filed by the Naletilic Defence which was raised with the Chamber this morning I indicated we would look at it. We have done so, Your Honour, and I am prepared to make an oral response which hopefully will both frame the matter a bit more quickly and perhaps at least save a page or two of paper. What I understand the proposal to be, and for the record I'm looking at the motion of the Naletilic Defence dated the 27th of June, submission concerning the schedule for finalising his case and commencement of the Martinovic Defence case, I've read the motion, I've also discussed it with Mr. Meek. Let me state what I think I understand it is so that I can decide it's clear what the Prosecution is agreeing to. The proposal is that there are six additional witnesses that will be called by the Naletilic Defence following the completion of the witnesses next week. My understanding that the remaining witnesses between now and next week or -- are a couple of fact witnesses and the last two witnesses will be two expert witnesses. It's my understanding from this submission and from Mr. Meek that following those witnesses, these six witnesses plus [redacted] will be the only, excuse me? Let's go to private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Let's go to private session.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Supreme Commander was a political figure. Defence department was also headed by a political figure. The head of the Main Staff was the Chief of the Main Staff, and for a while, the Main Staff also had a commander in addition to the chief. Under the Main Staff, he was in charge of operations and in charge of units for special purposes and professional units. As well as the units assigned to the Main Staff, which were mostly units for support and logistics. The Main Staff was directly in charge of the commands of the operation areas, or operation zones. Operation zones commanded units in their respective areas, and within that frame were ATGs with a lesser strength. Units of local character, which were not intended for maneuvers or not intended to leave their areas. I explained units for special purposes and ATGs -- and professional units yesterday.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please briefly repeat that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NP [Resumed]
utterances.text: During 1992, there were four. The Ante Bruno Busic regiment, the Ludvig Pavlovic, the Baja Kraljevic ATG, and the Convicts Battalion. Later on, in 1992, part of the Convicts Battalion was transferred and became an ATG. And part of it remained and was resubordinated to the Siroki Brijeg Brigade. There were other professional units but those were in Central Bosnia. Their commanders, however, were in -- on the ground, as well as the commanders of ATGs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And now can I kindly ask you, let's take the Rastani theatre. Where would Rastani belong, to which operation zone, and who was the commander of the Rastani theatre? And what was his relation to the Ludvig Pavlovic Battalion? Can you explain on this example to the Chamber, the chain of command?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NP [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Rastani theatre of war was within the operation zone Mostar. The operation zone Mostar had several sectors. Rastani belonged to the sector north. The commander at the time was Mr. Stampar. When the times were critical for him, he would turn to the commander of the operation zone, the operation zone would turn to the Main Staff, and if the Main Staff made a decision to engage any of the units, then the Main Staff would issue an order and send it to that particular zone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: I have to object. It seems to me that it's not re-examination, but a new direct examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, in this sense, I could not agree with you. I think it's a kind of clarification of the points raised by you during your cross-examination. We will allow the Defence counsel to continue to see where he is going to lead us.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NP [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Such practice did not exist. When I arrived, I was not familiar with the general front line. I was responsible for carrying out the task that I was given. But not for the execution of the task given to the entire sector. For the execution -- the commander of that sector was responsible for the execution of the task given to the entire sector.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And my final question: Was the practice the same for all operation zones when professional units or ATGs were sent to any of them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NP [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can say that this was so in these three operation zones, because I was sent there. I was never sent to Orasje.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Orasje is in Northern Bosnia or Posavina, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NP [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is Posavina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Let's move on. I would kindly ask the usher to give you Exhibit number P260.1. Sorry, P206.1. Can you please read the date in the left, upper corner?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NP [Resumed]
utterances.text: The date is 31 December, 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell us what the title of this document is? I apologise for asking you to read.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NP [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Report on the situation in the professional structure of the HVO."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who was this report submitted to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NP [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was sent to the head of the Defence department, Mr. Bruno Stojic, to the head of the Main Staff of the HVO, Brigadier Milivoj Petkovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please look at the second page and tell us who sent this document to them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NP [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was sent by the assistant Chief of the Main Staff of the HVO for the professional army, Colonel Ivica Primorac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The same gentleman whom you have mentioned in -- on both direct and cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NP [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please look at items 4 and 5? Which units are these and who is indicated as their commanders?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NP [Resumed]
utterances.text: Under 4, the Baja Kraljevic ATG, commander Predrag Mandic. Number 5, the Convicts Battalion, commander Mario Hrkac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was Mr. Mario Hrkac's nickname Cikota?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NP [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please turn to page number 2 and read items C and D?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NP [Resumed]
utterances.text: "C, the Convicts Battalion Mostar Heliodrom is a unit which gave a maximum contribution to the liberation of Mostar, is also ready to execute the most difficult tasks at any given time".

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... the parties should not read the documents in the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, no, I don't think we have made that decision, about but in this case it's indeed, Mr. Krsnik, there is no need for the witness to read the document, since everybody has one at their hands. So just draw our attention to certain paragraphs.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now let's move on to item D. You don't have to read. Do you -- can you see what it says under item D?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NP [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us whether the Convicts Battalion was ever located in the Heliodrom, to your knowledge, or if not, who was it that was located in the Heliodrom in 1992? I mean the professional unit. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NP [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to my knowledge, it was the Baja Kraljevic ATG that was stationed in the Heliodrom.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And to your knowledge, where was the Convicts Battalion situated?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NP [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Convicts Battalion was in Siroki Brijeg.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: According to your personal knowledge, does this reflect the truth, what it says here in this document?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NP [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to what I know, what I heard from the late Mario Cikota, this does not reflect the truth: The Convicts Battalion was not in Mostar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the rest of the document? Who was the commander of the two units? Were these two different units, the Convicts Battalion and the Baja Kraljevic? Were these two different units? Were they -- their commanders different people?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NP [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that the commander of the Convicts Battalion was Mr. Ivan Andabak and that Mario Hrkac was in charge of operations, that he was the one who was dealing with the operative matters. The Baja Kraljevic ATG, I don't know who the commander was, whether it was Predrag Mandic or Stanko Sopta.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Let's go to page 3. Under item 4, it says, "PPN, the Convicts Battalion." Does the number of men reflect the truth?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NP [Resumed]
utterances.text: I must admit that I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now can we have Exhibit P261? P261.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell the Chamber what Domovnica is and what -- why do you have to have a Domovnica in order to obtain what things?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NP [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Domovnica is the basic piece of document in the Republic of Croatia serving to prove that you are a citizen of the Republic of Croatia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So in order to obtain the citizenship of the Republic of Croatia, you first have to have the right to have a Domovnica; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NP [Resumed]
utterances.text: In order to deal with all your requirements, whatever you needed in the Republic of Croatia, you have to have a Domovnica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So in order to prove that you are a citizen of Croatia, would you say that the Domovnica is the necessary -- the only necessary prerequisite?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NP [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does it -- doesn't it say clearly in this document that people who are asking for Domovnica are not the citizens of the Republic of Croatia and that they are asking for a Domovnica?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: That's the best [RealTime transcript read in error "first"] example of the wrong way to pose a question so far.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: It was not allowed even at school.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: The transcript should read, "The best example."

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry, this is not my first mistake today. I have made another mistake in my re-examination. I am going to find it very difficult to correct that mistake, however. The witness is tired, I am tired, I would like to finish this examination. I have quite a number of questions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What I wanted to ask you is this: I don't know how to ask you. The document speaks for itself, I believe, so I will -- I guess I'll have to move on. Why do these people ask to be issued Domovnica? Is that now a better question?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NP [Resumed]
utterances.text: They are applying for Domovnica to -- in order to be entitled to the Croatian nationality.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Let's move on. P365.1. Will you now please have a good look at this signature, at the signature only, and tell us if it says anything, who signed this? I mean this typed thing. And then look at the signature and tell us what is this title here, the one that is indicated in the signature?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NP [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here, in front of chief "natalica" [phoen], there are two letters, Z-A, which mean "for." And then it is added the word "natalica" [phoen], there is a letter "A" added as a suffix which means "for the Chief of the Main Staff of the Croat Defence Council."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And whose name figures in the typed signature?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NP [Resumed]
utterances.text: Major General Milivoj Petkovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you read this handwritten, this writing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NP [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It looks like Ivica but I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Will you go back it 206.1 and look at the signature there? I believe you have this document, that it has not been taken away from you. We have it here, I believe you still have it with you. 261. You still have 261 with you? 261? The one that I asked you about Domovnica. Will you please compare these two signatures, the one that I just gave you. Are these three signatures -- can you read them -- can you read them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NP [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's the same signature. It's the same signature as on the report on the situation in the professional troops. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And this one on Domovnica 261, 206, no, 216, I'm sorry, 261, you're very quick. You remove documents very quickly, sorry.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NP [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. It is Ivica Primorac's signature. He signed on behalf of the Chief of the Main Staff of the HVO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could he do that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NP [Resumed]
utterances.text: He could do it, but in that case, it wasn't the proper order which one was duty-bound to comply with.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. Let's move on. Document 370.1, P370.1. The second passage which says the HVO has three special operations units, Tuta unit, which is dependent directly on Lasic, which might that "PB," the special unit on the 7th of May, 1993.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NP [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not know which unit they have in mind, unless it is Baja Kraljevic, because there were very many former members of the Convicts Battalion who -- and then some people still called them Tutici, Tuta's boys, they disagreed with that but at times we were called for instance at the time when we were with Daidza we were called Daidza's boys.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You testified for me yesterday, so I will ask you once again now on the 7th of May, 1993, did Mr. Naletilic have any command position in the HVO?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NP [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's move on. Document 374, please only one question because these are SpaBat reports. Did you see a single SFOR or whatever it was called, UNPROFOR soldier in Mostar on the 9th or the 10th?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NP [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not see anyone at the place where I was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell us how could he know who was firing from where unless they were on the scene?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes?

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Calls for speculation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krsnik, it's really speculation. Please remember, this is your re-examination. It's not your -- another chance for the direct examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I am not examining on the basis of these documents but all the documents were produced by the Prosecutor, and I am following these documents and I'm requiring -- I'm requesting additional information from -- regarding these documents which were produced by the Prosecution. Perhaps the Prosecution is not interested in that but I am because I want to know the truth. I agree that this is speculation and of course what it says in here is also speculation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now -- now document 376.1. Sorry, 376.1. I'm sorry, witness, that I keep you so long but there are certain things that I'd like to clarify. All I want to know is who signed this. Will you please read like in that other document?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NP [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document was signed by somebody on behalf of the commander, Miljenko Lasic because it says, "For" Z-A, for the commander.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you read it have a good look?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NP [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe the signature was Petar Zelenika.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who was that commander? Would he sign it at the time? Look at the date.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NP [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think he could not do it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think the name Zelenika was not mentioned during the cross-examination and again, it's pure speculation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Krsnik, I believe that it is speculation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But Your Honours, with all due respect, I do not allow -- I apologise but do not allow the Prosecutor to do to me, I won't say what. Your Honours, I see what it says here. I can read it. It's in the Croatian language. I see the signature. I'm not a fool. I'm asking the witness whether he knows who Petar Zelenika is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know Petar Zelenika?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NP [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what duty he -- what post he held on the 9th of May, 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NP [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know exactly what post he held but I do not think that he could sign on behalf of Brigadier Lasic because there was also Stanko, I don't know what his last name is, Stanko Puljic who came right next after Miljenko Lasic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, please tell me, this is the personal signature. Read in your Croatian language what you can, what does this handwritten signature, this own signature, what does it say?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Mr. Krsnik, is this the right witness to be asking this? Isn't the person coming next week who we can ask? So why are you asking this witness to talk about something that he can only speculate about? I can ask my secretary to sign letters. If my secretary is on holidays I can ask a stand-in for a day to sign letters. And so can you. I mean, the appropriate person to ask is either the person who signed the letter or the person who gave authority to sign the letter, not this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, you're absolutely right. All I want, because any Irishman -- I apologise. I believe any Irish man would be able to read your signature if it were as legible as this one and I ask the witness to read what was written here. Secondly, Your Honour, this witness is qualified to a say that because orders are issued to him by Mr. Lasic and he must know who is authorised to sign orders because he must know who issues the orders, and he's been testifying for two days about that, so if somebody had to know that then it is this witness. Am I not right when I say that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NP [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've just said that this order was ridiculous, that it could not be a serious order.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that is why I asked you in redirect because that was what you said to the Prosecutor. Let's move on. Could we have document P564.1? I'm interested only in item 2 of this document. The Prosecutor asked you questions about that. And my question to you is: According to your personal knowledge, and in particular since you were assistant to the chief of the Main Staff for professional units, was there a Tuta ATG?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NP [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. In the official documents there was never mention of Tuta ATG. There was the Convicts Battalion, there was the Convicts Battalion, but the ATG, no Tuta ATG existed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And tell me, will you turn to page 2? If you know, and it says commander of the Main Staff of the HVO, and should be the man issuing orders to you. Is this General Slobodan Praljak's signature?

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: The author of this signature gave his testimony in this courtroom, and he acknowledged his signature. The document was admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. We could compare the signature of this document with others.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is not true. That is not true, Your Honours. How can such things be said in this courtroom? Mr. General Praljak never said it was his signature and that's what this is all about.
